For the Petitioner : Mr. Gautam Kumar Singh, Advocate. For the State : Mr. Shailesh Kumar Sinha,
A.P.P.
For the O.P. No. 2 : Mr. Din Dayal Saha, Advocate.
th Order No. 05/Dated: 12 March, 2024 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Apprehending his arrest in connection with Complaint Case No. 213 of 2022, instituted under Sections 323 / 498A of the I.P.C. and Section 3 / 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, the petitioner has moved to this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.

As per the complaint, the allegation is that the marriage of complainant was solemnized with the petitioner on 09.02.2020 and after three months of marriage, an illegal demand of additional dowry was made and on non-fulfillment of the same, she was subjected to torture.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is submitted that petitioner is the husband of the complainant and there is general and omnibus allegation against all the accused persons.
It is further submitted that vide order dated 06.10.2022, cognizance has been taken against the petitioner under Sections 323/ 498A of the I.P.C. and Section 3 / 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
It is a complaint case, as such, there is no requirement of custodial trial of the petitioner.
It is further submitted that petitioner shall abide by all terms and conditions imposed by this Court in the matter of granting anticipatory bail.
Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.

Learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State assisted by learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner and has submitted that there is no chance of conciliation.
Petitioner could not keep his wife with due honour and dignity and there is serious allegation against the petitioner.

Hence, petitioner does not deserve the privilege of anticipatory Amit Kumar Sah vs The State Of Jharkhand & Another ..... ... on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132540947/

sentences.text: Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of allegation against petitioner coupled with materials available on record, I am inclined to extend privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to surrender in the Court within four weeks from today and in the event of his arrest or surrendering, he will be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.20,000/- (Twenty thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned J.M., 1st Class, Rajmahal in connection with Complaint Case No. 213 of 2022 subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
